Introduction

This is the story of how Canadians have sought to improve their health in the face of many challenges and uncertainties. The chapters that follow trace the evolution of health care in Canada since the earliest days of settlement. We begin with a look at the health of Aboriginal peoples in what is now Canada, and at the dramatic changes that occurred with the arrival of Europeans. The story continues with an account of the rise and fall of epidemics, and of the growth of government involvement in the health of Canadians. We then examine the development of hospitals and health professionals, as well as the role of drugs, medical technology, and other therapies. Finally, we look at the major reports that have led to health care reform in the 20th century, and at the continuing challenges facing Canadians in the new millennium. Our health is influenced by a complex array of factors. These include the physical environment, the food we eat, the amount of physical activity we engage in, our employment situation, and our access to health care. These factors in turn are affected by a wide range of forces, including the economy, our personal choices, and the actions of governments, corporations, and other organizations. The story of health care in Canada is complex and multi-faceted. Our intention is not to provide a comprehensive or definitive account, but rather to stimulate readers to explore this story further through their own research and reading. The chapters that follow are written in non-technical language, and are designed to be accessible to a broad range of readers. We hope that this book will be used by students, teachers, and the general public, as well as by health professionals, government officials, and others concerned with the health of Canadians. There are many ways to tell a story, and many different perspectives one can adopt in telling it. We have chosen to tell our story mainly from a Canadian point of view. That is, we focus primarily on the development of health care in Canada, although we also look at the influence of major international events and trends, including the impact of global health issues and the rise of the global economy. We also draw on the work of historians, sociologists, anthropologists, economists, political scientists, and other scholars to provide a wide-ranging and interdisciplinary approach to the story of health care in Canada. This book is designed to be used in a variety of ways. It can be read in its entirety, or used as a resource for specific topics or themes. Each chapter includes a brief overview, a list of key concepts and terms, a list of further readings, and a set of questions and activities. The questions and activities are designed to encourage readers to explore the story of health care in Canada further, through their own research and reading. We hope that this book will stimulate readers to think critically about the challenges and opportunities facing Canadians in the new millennium. The story of health care in Canada is an ongoing one, and there is much that remains to be told.
